nodes.name: Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office
nodes.note: Held Epstein for about 13 months (2008-09), most of it on work release: up to 12 hours a day, six days a week, outside the jail. In 2019 the sheriff opened an internal inquiry, handed it to the state, and ended the work-release programme.

nodes.name: Ric Bradshaw
nodes.note: Palm Beach County sheriff. Asked in 2019 for the state (FDLE) to take over oversight of his office's review of Epstein's custody.

nodes.name: Florida Department of Law Enforcement
nodes.note: Asked by Gov. DeSantis in August 2019 to review the state case, the plea and the custody. Reported in 2021: no evidence of criminal activity by officials and no evidence the State Attorney colluded with the defence; it found "differential treatment" in custody and that sex during work release was "possible" but not provable.

nodes.name: Ron DeSantis
nodes.note: Florida governor. Asked FDLE to review the state's handling of the Epstein case (August 2019); signed the 2024 law allowing release of the 2006 grand jury testimony.

nodes.name: Palm Beach County grand jury (2006)
nodes.note: Heard the state case in 2006 and returned a single solicitation charge. Its testimony was released in July 2024 under the new state law.

nodes.name: Florida grand jury disclosure law (2024)
nodes.note: Passed unanimously and signed on 29 Feb 2024 (Senate sponsor Tina Polsky); in force 1 Jul 2024. Widened the exception to grand-jury secrecy so the 2006 Epstein testimony could be released.

nodes.name: Judge Luis Delgado
nodes.note: Palm Beach circuit judge. In February 2024 held the request until the new law took effect; the transcripts were then released.

nodes.name: Manhattan District Attorney's Office
nodes.note: At Epstein's 2011 New York sex-offender hearing, an assistant DA conceded he should be rated level one, the lowest risk; the judge rated him level three, and the appeals court said the concession was a mistake.

nodes.name: Justice Ruth Pickholz
nodes.note: New York Supreme Court justice. Rated Epstein a level three sex offender in 2011, over the DA's concession of level one; affirmed on appeal.

nodes.name: People v Epstein (New York sex-offender level, 2011)
nodes.note: Appellate Division, First Department, 17 Nov 2011: unanimously affirmed level three. He was rated level one in Florida and the US Virgin Islands.

nodes.name: New York Police Department
nodes.note: Required 90-day address checks for a level three offender; Epstein never checked in. He had listed the Virgin Islands as his primary residence and New York as a vacation home, and the NYPD held that his monitoring was not its responsibility.

nodes.name: New Mexico registry gap
nodes.note: Epstein was not required to register in New Mexico: the Florida victim in his plea was 17, the state's age of consent. After his 2019 arrest the attorney general sought to make any sex-trafficking conviction registrable.

nodes.name: New York Child Victims Act (2019)
nodes.note: Opened a one-year window, from 14 Aug 2019, for claims that had expired; suits against Epstein's estate were filed on the first day.

nodes.name: Estate of Jeffrey Epstein
nodes.note: Executors Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn. Funded the victims' compensation programme (2020); settled with the US Virgin Islands for $105M (Dec 2022), forfeiting the islands' sale proceeds in part to a victims' trust; sold every property 2021-23.

nodes.name: Denise George
nodes.note: US Virgin Islands attorney general, May 2019 to Dec 2022. Sued the estate (2020; $105M settlement, Dec 2022) and filed suit against JPMorgan on 27 Dec 2022; dismissed four days later. Her later account to the FBI (released Jan 2026) is her allegation.

nodes.name: Albert Bryan
nodes.note: US Virgin Islands governor. Appointed and then dismissed Attorney General Denise George on 31 Dec 2022, saying he had been "blindsided" by the JPMorgan suit filed without consulting him.

nodes.name: Judge Richard M. Berman
nodes.note: SDNY judge in the 2019 case. Denied bail on 18 Jul 2019, finding Epstein a danger to the community and a flight risk, against a bail package offered against his Manhattan house.
